$comment: Every word of the first run, on the Mac (src/components/FirstRun.tsx, src/lib/first-run.ts) and on the iPhone (OnboardingView.swift, ParkerCore FirstRunText). One file, so the two apps say the same thing. A key ending in @mac or @iphone is that app's version of the key without it; {name} is filled in by the app; **bold** and [links](url) are markdown. Both test suites check every key they use is here, and shared/fixtures/first-run-lines.json holds the sentences built from it.

strings.welcome.title: Hi, I'm Parker.
strings.welcome.lead: Your notes are plain Markdown files in one folder. Any app, and any AI agent, can read them.
strings.welcome.look@mac: I'll look for them in **Documents › Parker**. macOS will ask you once.
strings.welcome.look@iphone: I'll look for them in **{home}**. On the next screen, tap **Open**.
strings.welcome.driveOff: iCloud Drive is off on this iPhone.
strings.welcome.driveOffDetail: Turn it on to keep your notes in sync with your Mac.
strings.welcome.driveOn: iCloud Drive is on. Your notes will sync.
strings.welcome.otherApp@iphone: Parker for Mac is free at [getparker.dev](https://getparker.dev).
strings.welcome.terms: By continuing you accept the [terms](https://getparker.dev/terms) and [privacy policy](https://getparker.dev/privacy).
strings.denied.title: No problem.
strings.denied.lead@mac: I can't look in Documents. Choose any folder for your notes, or allow access and try again.
strings.denied.lead@iphone: I can't see iCloud Drive yet. Try again and tap **Open**, or choose any folder for your notes.
strings.denied.detail@mac: System Settings › Privacy & Security › Files & Folders › Parker.
strings.found.title: Found your notes.
strings.create.title: A fresh start.
strings.create.lead: No notes yet. I'll create **{folder}** with a Welcome note.
strings.create.arriving@mac: Used Parker on another device? iCloud may still be bringing that folder here.
strings.arriving.title: Almost there.
strings.arriving.lead: iCloud is still bringing your notes to this {device}. Wait a moment and try again, so you don't end up with two folders.
strings.setup.title: Here's your setup.
strings.setup.updated@mac: Desktop & Documents is on. Your notes will sync.
strings.setup.recommend@mac: Turn on **Desktop & Documents** in iCloud settings to sync this folder. This screen updates when you come back. It puts your whole Documents folder in iCloud Drive, which counts toward your storage.
strings.setup.otherWaysBody: Parker doesn't sync anything itself. On the Mac, any service that syncs a folder works: Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, Box and others.
strings.setup.otherWaysHow@mac: Keep your notes folder inside that service's folder and choose it here. On the iPhone, the service's app has to let other apps open its folders: Dropbox does, Box doesn't. iCloud Drive always works.
strings.setup.otherWaysHow@iphone: Install the service's app, then use Choose another folder. Not every app lets others open its folders: Dropbox does, Box doesn't. On the Mac, choose the same folder in Parker.
strings.help.title: Where is my folder?
strings.help.step1: On your Mac, open Parker and look at Settings › Notes folder.
strings.help.step2: If that folder is in iCloud Drive, choose the same folder here. Your notes appear in seconds.
strings.help.step3: If your Mac keeps Desktop & Documents in iCloud, the folder is under iCloud Drive › Documents.
strings.help.note: A folder in On My iPhone stays on this phone and doesn't sync with your Mac.
strings.dev.message@iphone: “{folder}” doesn't look like a dev folder. A build like this one can rewrite notes while a feature is half done. Choose a folder with “Dev” in its name, like the one Parker Dev uses on the Mac.
strings.line.state.new: New. I'll create it when you continue.
strings.line.state.empty: Empty. I'll add a Welcome note.
strings.line.state.onlyOther: {other}, no notes yet. I leave those files alone.
strings.line.sync.icloudDriveOff@mac: In iCloud Drive, but iCloud Drive is off on this Mac.
strings.line.sync.icloudDriveOff@iphone: iCloud Drive is off on this iPhone.
strings.line.sync.here@mac: Stays on this Mac. Documents isn't in iCloud.
strings.line.sync.hereDriveOff@mac: Stays on this Mac. iCloud Drive is off.
strings.line.sync.hereDriveOff@iphone: Stays on this iPhone. iCloud Drive is off.
strings.line.sync.anyService@iphone: Syncs with a cloud service, not iCloud Drive.
strings.line.sync.unknown: Not in iCloud Drive. If it syncs another way, see Other ways to sync.
strings.line.git.note@mac: I can commit and push your changes. Turn it on in Settings › Backup & Git.
strings.line.git.noteICloud@mac: I can commit and push your changes. Turn it on in Settings › Backup & Git. iCloud can duplicate files inside .git, so keep an eye on it.
strings.line.git.note@iphone: Your Mac commits and pushes. I just edit the notes.
strings.line.git.noneNote@mac: Optional. Make it one later and I can commit and push it.
strings.line.git.noneNote@iphone: Optional. Parker for Mac can make it one.
strings.line.other.suggested@mac: Install Parker for iPhone and tap Continue with iCloud Drive. It finds this folder by itself.
strings.line.other.suggestedOff@mac: Your iPhone can't reach it yet. Turn on Desktop & Documents, then tap Continue with iCloud Drive on the iPhone.
strings.line.other.icloud@mac: In Parker for iPhone, tap Choose another folder and pick {folder}.
strings.line.other.icloudDriveOff@mac: Turn on iCloud Drive on this Mac first, or your iPhone won't see your notes. Then, in Parker for iPhone, tap Choose another folder and pick {folder}.
strings.line.other.service@mac: Install the {service} app, then in Parker for iPhone tap Choose another folder and pick {folder}.
strings.line.other.anyService@mac: If {service} has an iPhone app, install it, then in Parker for iPhone tap Choose another folder and pick {folder}.
strings.line.other.here@mac: Your iPhone can't reach it while Documents stays on this Mac.
strings.line.other.unknown@mac: If this folder stays on this Mac, your iPhone can't open it.
strings.line.other.suggested@iphone: Install Parker for Mac. It finds this folder by itself if the Mac keeps Documents in iCloud, and shows how to turn that on if it doesn't.
strings.line.other.icloud@iphone: In Parker for Mac, choose this folder: {folder}.
strings.line.other.service@iphone: Install {service} on the Mac, then choose this folder in Parker: {folder}.
strings.line.other.here@iphone: Your Mac can't reach a folder that stays on this iPhone. Turn on iCloud Drive to share it.
strings.line.other.unknown@iphone: If this folder stays on this iPhone, your Mac can't open it.
strings.line.other.anyService@iphone: Install the same service on the Mac, then choose this folder in Parker: {folder}.
